title: Zechariah 11:15–17
context: The LORD tells the prophet to take up the equipment of a foolish shepherd, as a sign of a shepherd the LORD will raise up who neglects the lost, the scattered, the broken, and the sound, and instead devours the flock. A woe follows against the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock: the sword will strike his arm and his right eye. Ezekiel 34 likewise condemns shepherds who feed themselves rather than the sheep. The identity of the foolish shepherd is uncertain, and readers have proposed both particular leaders and a type of false shepherd.  Some connect this figure with the shepherd of 13:7, while many read 13:7 as a good shepherd close to the LORD; the relationship is named without being forced. Shared ground: both traditions read the passage as a sober warning against leaders who exploit those in their care.

verses.text: The LORD said to me, “Take for yourself yet again the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD said to me, Arminian readers see the prophet commanded to act out a second role, taking the equipment of a foolish shepherd as a sign of leaders to come.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the equipment is not described in detail. The foolish shepherd represents a leader who lacks the wisdom and care required for the flock.

verses.text: For, behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not visit those who are cut off, neither will seek those who are scattered, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which is sound; but he will eat the meat of the fat sheep, and will tear their hoofs in pieces.
verses.arminianNotes: For, behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not visit those who are cut off, Arminian readers see the LORD allowing a harmful leader to arise as judgment on a people who rejected the good shepherd.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers compare Ezekiel 34:2-4, which lists the same failures to heal, seek, and feed. The identity of the shepherd is uncertain, and the verse is described soberly.

verses.text: Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! The sword will strike his arm and his right eye. His arm will be completely withered, and his right eye will be totally blinded!”
verses.arminianNotes: Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! Arminian readers see judgment falling on the shepherd who abandons the flock, his arm withered and his right eye blinded.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the arm and eye picture strength and perception, both taken away. John 10:12 also contrasts the true shepherd with one who leaves the sheep.
